complacency

/kuhm-PLAY-suhn-see/ - the stress falls on PLAY · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Complacency means self-satisfied contentment that blinds a person to danger.

Two centuries without a flood left the levee board sunk in complacency; the sandbags in the depot had rotted, and nobody had checked.

Example

The driving school's toughest lecture is aimed not at new students but at ten-year veterans. Crashes spike, the instructor explains, exactly when drivers decide they have seen everything: mirror checks get skipped, following distances shrink, and the habits that kept them safe dissolve — not from ignorance, but from complacency.

Complacency is more precise than overconfidence here because it names the mechanism: a self-satisfied comfort that quietly switches off vigilance. The overconfident driver overrates his skill; the complacent one may truly be skilled — he has simply stopped watching.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

smugness: Smugness is being pleased with yourself at others' expense — it adds an air of superiority and needs someone to look down on. Complacency needs no audience at all: it is the private comfort of believing nothing can go wrong, satisfaction that quietly stops checking.

overconfidence: Overconfidence is overrating your own ability — believing you can do more than you truly can. Complacency can infect the genuinely skilled: the complacent veteran may be excellent and has simply stopped watching. Overconfidence misjudges the self; complacency misjudges the risk, assuming danger has retired.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

wariness: alert caution that keeps on checking

alarm: the jolt of sensing danger right now

Where it sits · how blind to danger the comfort grows — contentment → complacency → hubris

contentment vs. complacency: Contentment is satisfaction with eyes still open; complacency goes further — satisfaction so comfortable it stops looking for trouble.

hubris vs. complacency: Hubris outruns complacency: the complacent titleholder merely skips practice, while hubris taunts the challenger and bets the crown on it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — com-

Prefix — com-: thoroughly, with

Root — plac

Root — plac: to please (Latin placere)

Suffix — -ency

Suffix — -ency: state of

Put it together

Put it together: Com- (thoroughly) + plac (to please) + -ency (state of) = the state of being thoroughly pleased — with yourself. Latin complacere meant 'to please greatly'; English narrowed it to the dangerous kind of self-pleasure that stops checking the locks.

Use the root in a new word: pleasant

Use the root in a new word: pleasant: A pleasant breeze off the lake kept the hikers cool through the whole climb.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / critical

Complacency always carries a warning label: the comfort it names is the kind that comes before a fall. Plain contentment is innocent; complacency is contentment asleep on watch duty. Where its cluster-mate indifferent means you never cared, the complacent person cares — he has just stopped believing anything could go wrong.
